what: FormFactor makes probe cards: the precision test fixtures that touch a silicon wafer's circuits to check whether each chip works before it is cut from the wafer. It also sells test systems and engineering probes used in semiconductor laboratories.
customers: Semiconductor manufacturers and foundries: memory makers, logic chip companies and the test houses that screen chips before packaging. Every chip design needs its own probe card.
money: Custom test cards for DRAM, flash memory, logic and system-on-chip devices.
Engineering probe stations, thermal subsystems and metrology tools for laboratories and production.
moat: Probe cards are designed for one specific chip layout, so they must be ordered from someone who can make thousands of contacts land within microns on a wafer. FormFactor is the largest supplier and its cards must be qualified with each customer's process, which takes months. Every new chip design generates a new order, which ties revenue to the pace of design activity rather than only to volumes.
risks: Revenue has been flat for years: $769.7M in 2021, $663.1M in 2023 and $785.0M in 2025, so the company has not grown through a period when semiconductor spending rose sharply.
The shares trade at about 37 times earnings and 6.5 times sales, which assumes growth that has not yet appeared.
Ten analysts average a $144.70 target against an $81.89 price, a 77% gap that deserves scepticism.
Memory chip demand is the largest end market and is the most cyclical part of semiconductors.
Technoprobe and other competitors have taken share in advanced logic probe cards, the fastest-growing segment.
opportunities: High-bandwidth memory for AI accelerators requires more test per wafer than conventional memory, which raises probe card demand per unit of silicon.
The balance sheet is very clean: $275.2M of cash against $32.4M of debt.
Advanced packaging, where several chips are combined in one module, requires testing at more stages, which expands the market.
Free cash flow of $181.3M on $980.1M of revenue is a reasonable conversion for a capital-equipment supplier.
watch: Probe card revenue from advanced logic and high-bandwidth memory. The overall figure has been flat; whether FormFactor is winning in the two segments that are actually growing is what decides the stock.
